_doc: Every game system PalCraft touches. One row = one system. owner = which game decides; channels refers to channels.json; code = the file that implements the row ('-' = none in this version).
rows: ReceiveTick hook runs the bridge each frame
CameraActor view target follows Control pose
clears one of 16 tiny render targets per tick
draws world, hand and HUD layers at Present
finds the scene depth buffer for occlusion
hidden character is carried to Steve, held still
line traces answer rays; hills solid from outside
lists nearby Pals with position, box, HP
CombatBridge queues sword, arrow, TNT hits
counts deaths and respawns both ways
F8 in Palworld asks Minecraft to take over
Overlay window glued over the Palworld one
gives kit.json once per player; newer kit waves top up an older kit
reports which parts came alive in a Melty test
mutes the system-info library's warnings about Windows counters
lifts Steve out when terrain fills in around him
names the surface one ray hits: soil, grass, stone, wood, sand, snow or ore
holding attack on Palworld's world digs it: drops by surface and tool
a Pal that Steve kills drops meat, hide, bones and XP; an alpha drops an enchanted golden apple
keeps its mouse pointer hidden while Minecraft holds the mouse
sends the sharpest layers that keep Minecraft above frame_min_fps
takes Steve's food as its stomach and his fires as heat sources; reports body temperature
sends food level and nearby warmth once a second
temperature gauge above the hunger bar, frost on the screen when cold; the bundled AppleSkin draws saturation
finds fire, torches, water and ice around Steve; leather armor counts as warmth
a Pal's hit goes through Minecraft's armor, toughness, Protection and shield rules and wears the armor; cold, heat and poison go past armor as in Minecraft
the old recipe is back: eight gold blocks around an apple make an enchanted golden apple
saves the PalCraft world every autosave_s seconds and the moment Palworld goes away, because the launcher may stop Minecraft without asking

in Palworld mode its own camera leads, shown a few frames late so Minecraft can match it: the character stays the view target (dialogue and cutscene cameras need that) with its follow camera cut loose from the arm and posed each tick; the character stays hidden, with the tool in its hand and the one stowed on its back, and keeps moving its bones, so the tool in its hand still sweeps through what it hits

draws Steve where the character stands, walking with it, and leaves him out while a wall pushes the camera against his back; his hands are empty there, as Palworld's tools do the work; when the character is defeated he falls over in its place; Steve takes no Minecraft damage meanwhile
a Pal that Steve's hit kills gives the Palworld character experience by its level; reports level and experience earned
shows the experience above the hotbar and a level-up message

Palworld mode, while Palworld shows a shot of its own (a conversation, a cutscene): publishes that shot's camera and lets Steve be drawn into it when Minecraft's frame matches; a fast-moving shot shows Palworld's own character
renders Steve from the shot's camera
draws the Minecraft layers right after the scene reaches the back buffer, so Palworld's menus, HUD and name tags land on top; falls back to drawing at Present
when Palworld's window has been gone for 20 seconds, saves the world and closes Minecraft, whose window nobody could see or reach

Palworld mode: fades its own health, hunger and temperature gauges, its level display and the stat-point banner that sits where the hotbar goes; keeps its prompts, compass, Pal party, key guides and boss bars; reports the character's health and whether a shot, menu, build mode or screen of its own is up

draws its HUD in Palworld mode: hearts show the character's health, the hunger bar its stomach and the experience bar its Palworld level; its crosshair marks the middle of the picture, where Palworld aims, in Palworld mode and behind Steve in Minecraft mode's third person; no block outline in Palworld mode, as Steve's hands are Palworld's there; holds the HUD back over Palworld's cutscenes, conversations, menus, build mode and defeat screen; says in chat when a new level brought points to spend
Palworld mode: reports the tools in its weapon slots, the one in hand with its rounds, and the selected Pal Sphere with its count; fades its own weapon panel

its hotbar shows them as Minecraft items in the slots Palworld's number keys pick, the sphere in the last slot while any is left, and marks the one in hand (the sphere while Steve aims one); rounds loaded are that slot's count, rounds carried stand beside the hotbar
fades the character preview of its inventory screen and says while it is up
draws Steve where that preview was and says where; Palworld draws its screens over Minecraft's picture, so the native compositor draws that part of Minecraft's HUD layer once more, over the interface
